---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API using a bot token: post messages and replies, list channels and users, read channel history, create channels, and upload files. Use when the user asks to send Slack messages, reply in threads, check Slack activity, manage channels, upload files to Slack, or automate Slack communication.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Send messages, reply in threads, list channels and users, read history, create channels, and upload files through the Slack Web API using a bot token. All operations go through `scripts/slack_api.py` (Python 3, stdlib only — no dependencies), which handles auth, channel-name resolution, pagination, and clean, concise output.

## Setup

- A Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) is required. Set it as the `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable or pass `--token`.
- The bot needs OAuth scopes for each operation; the required scopes are listed in [references/api.md](references/api.md).
- Verify the token quickly with `test` (calls `auth.test`).

## Quick Start

```bash
export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-...

# Verify the token works
python3 scripts/slack_api.py test

# Post a message
python3 scripts/slack_api.py post --channel general --text "Hello from the bot!"

# Reply inside a thread
python3 scripts/slack_api.py reply --channel general --thread-ts 1234567890.123456 --text "Replying in thread"

# List channels (paginated)
python3 scripts/slack_api.py list-channels

# Read recent messages from a channel
python3 scripts/slack_api.py history --channel general --limit 5

# Upload a file to a channel
python3 scripts/slack_api.py upload --channel general --file ./report.pdf --title "Monthly report"

# Create a channel
python3 scripts/slack_api.py create-channel --name announcements
```

## Script Reference (scripts/slack_api.py)

Run `python3 scripts/slack_api.py --help` for full usage. All subcommands accept `--token <token>` (overrides `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`) and `--dry-run` (print the request without sending — useful for previewing and testing without a token).

| Command | Slack endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `test` | auth.test | Verify the token and show the bot identity |
| `post --channel <name\|C...> --text <msg> [--thread-ts <ts>]` | chat.postMessage | Send a message (optionally in a thread) |
| `reply --channel <name\|C...> --thread-ts <ts> --text <msg>` | chat.postMessage | Reply inside a thread |
| `list-channels [--limit N] [--types <types>]` | conversations.list | List channels (paginated) |
| `history --channel <name\|C...> [--limit N]` | conversations.history | Read recent messages (newest first) |
| `users [--limit N]` | users.list | List workspace users (paginated) |
| `upload --channel <name\|C...> --file <path> [--title <t>] [--filename <n>] [--initial-comment <c>]` | files.getUploadURLExternal + files.completeUploadExternal | Upload a file to a channel (current two-step flow) |
| `create-channel --name <name> [--private]` | conversations.create | Create a public or private channel |

Channel arguments accept a name (`general`, `#general`) or an encoded ID (`C...`); names are resolved to IDs automatically via `conversations.list`.

## Behavior & Output

- Every command prints a single concise JSON object on stdout (e.g. `{"ok": true, "channel": "C123", "ts": "1234567890.123456"}`) so results can be parsed by an agent or script.
- Failures print `Failure: <slack error code or message>` to stderr and exit with code 1. No stack traces.
- `list-channels` and `users` follow `response_metadata.next_cursor` automatically until all pages are fetched.
- When the bot lacks a scope, the Slack error (e.g. `not_authorized`) is reported so the right scope can be added to the app.

## Message Formatting

Messages use mrkdwn by default: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|label>` links, `:tada:` emoji, `<@U123>` user mentions, `<#C123>` channel links.

## Detailed Reference

For endpoint parameters, required OAuth scopes per endpoint, rate limits, error codes, pagination details, and Slack API limits, read [references/api.md](references/api.md). Read it when a task needs an endpoint not listed above, when debugging scope/error issues, or when formatting complex messages.

# Slack Web API Reference

Reference for common Slack Web API operations used by the `slack-api` skill. Read this when a task needs an endpoint not covered in SKILL.md, when debugging scope/error issues, or when formatting complex messages.

## Table of Contents

1. [Authentication & tokens](#1-authentication--tokens)
2. [Common endpoints](#2-common-endpoints)
3. [Required OAuth scopes](#3-required-oauth-scopes)
4. [Message formatting (mrkdwn)](#4-message-formatting-mrkdwn)
5. [Pagination](#5-pagination)
6. [Rate limits](#6-rate-limits)
7. [Errors & troubleshooting](#7-errors--troubleshooting)
8. [API limits](#8-api-limits)

## 1. Authentication & Tokens

- Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`, app-level tokens with `xapp-`.
- Send the token as an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on every request.
- Verify a token with `auth.test` (returns `bot_id`, `user`, `team`, `url`).
- Tokens are workspace-scoped; a token from one workspace cannot access another.
- Bot tokens act as the bot user; user tokens (`xoxp-`) act as the user and require `chat:write` with user token scopes.

## 2. Common Endpoints

All methods: `POST https://slack.com/api/<method>` with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body. Response is always JSON with an `ok` field.

### chat.postMessage

| Param | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `channel` | yes | Channel ID (`C...`) or name; script resolves names automatically |
| `text` | yes | mrkdwn-formatted; max 40,000 chars |
| `thread_ts` | no | Parent message ts → posts a reply in that thread |
| `mrkdwn` | no | Set `false` to disable formatting |
| `link_names` | no | `true` to linkify `@username` and channel names |
| `blocks` | no | JSON array of Block Kit blocks (max 100) |
| `reply_broadcast` | no | `true` to also post thread reply to the channel (only with `thread_ts`) |

Returns `ts` (message timestamp, used for threads) and `channel`. Scope: `chat:write`.

### conversations.list

| Param | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `types` | no | Comma list: `public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im` (default `public_channel`) |
| `limit` | no | 1–200, default 100 |
| `cursor` | no | Pagination cursor |
| `exclude_archived` | no | `true` to hide archived channels |

Returns `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_private`, `is_archived`, `num_members`. Scopes depend on `types`: `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`.

### conversations.history

| Param | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `channel` | yes | Channel ID |
| `limit` | no | 1–999, default 100 |
| `cursor` | no | Pagination cursor |
| `oldest` / `latest` | no | Unix timestamps in seconds (or ts strings) to bound the range |
| `inclusive` | no | Include boundary messages |

Returns `messages[]` newest-first, each with `ts`, `user` or `bot_id`, `text`, optional `thread_ts`, `reply_count`. Scope: `channels:history` (plus `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` per channel type).

### conversations.replies

| Param | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `channel` | yes | Channel ID |
| `ts` | yes | Parent message ts of the thread |

Returns the parent message plus all replies. Scope: same as history (`channels:history` etc.).

### conversations.create

| Param | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Lowercase, no spaces, max 80 chars |
| `is_private` | no | `true` for a private channel |

Returns the created `channel`. Scopes: `channels:manage` (public), `groups:write` (private). Errors: `name_taken`, `invalid_name`, `restricted_action`.

### users.list

| Param | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | no | 1–200, default 100 |
| `cursor` | no | Pagination cursor |

Returns `members[]` with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `is_bot`, `deleted`. Scope: `users:read`.

### File upload (current two-step flow)

Legacy `files.upload` (single call) is deprecated — use the two-step flow:

1. `POST files.getUploadURLExternal` — params: `filename` (required), `length` (required, bytes), `alt_txt`. Returns `upload_url` and `file_id`.
2. `PUT` the raw file bytes to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`.
3. `POST files.completeUploadExternal` — params: `files` (JSON string array, e.g. `[{"id":"F123","title":"report.pdf"}]`), `channel_id`, optional `initial_comment`, `thread_ts`.

Scope: `files:write`. Max upload: 1 GB. If `channel_id` is omitted, the file is shared with the bot only.

## 3. Required OAuth Scopes

| Endpoint | Bot scopes |
|---|---|
| `auth.test` | none |
| `chat.postMessage` | `chat:write` |
| `conversations.list` | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` (per `types`) |
| `conversations.history` / `conversations.replies` | `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` (per channel type) |
| `conversations.create` | `channels:manage` (public) / `groups:write` (private) |
| `users.list` | `users:read` |
| `files.getUploadURLExternal` / `files.completeUploadExternal` | `files:write` |

If the bot is not in a private channel, it cannot read/write it regardless of scopes — add the bot to the channel or use `conversations.invite` with `channels:manage`.

## 4. Message Formatting (mrkdwn)

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, ``` ```pre``` ``` (triple backticks)
- Link: `<https://example.com>`; labeled link: `<https://example.com|label>`
- User mention: `<@U123>`; channel link: `<#C123>`; special: `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>`
- Emoji: `:tada:`, `:white_check_mark:`
- Newlines: use `\n`; paragraph breaks with `\n\n`
- To escape special chars, prefix with a backslash: `\<`, `\&` (escape `&` as `&` is not needed in text)

## 5. Pagination

- Responses include `response_metadata.next_cursor`; an empty string means the last page.
- Pass the cursor back as the `cursor` param for the next page.
- The `slack_api.py` script follows pagination automatically for `list-channels` and `users`.
- `conversations.history` also paginates; the script returns one page per `--limit`.

## 6. Rate Limits

- Per-method rate limits depend on the app's tier: Tier 1 (new apps) ~1 req/min/method; Tier 2 ~20/min; Tier 3 ~50/min; Tier 4 ~100/min. `auth.test` and a few methods have higher limits.
- On throttling: HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Back off and retry.
- Batch operations (e.g. posting to many channels) should add small delays to stay under limits.

## 7. Errors & Troubleshooting

Slack returns HTTP 200 with `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>"}` for normal API errors — check `ok` first.

| Error | Meaning / fix |
|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Token is invalid or revoked |
| `not_authorized` | Bot lacks the required OAuth scope → add scope to the app and reinstall |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel doesn't exist or bot is not a member (private channels) |
| `is_archived` | Cannot post to an archived channel |
| `name_taken` / `invalid_name` | Channel name conflict or invalid |
| `thread_not_found` | `thread_ts` doesn't exist in that channel |
| `rate_limited` | Slow down; respect `Retry-After` |
| `account_inactive` | Workspace or bot deactivated |
| `too_many_attachments` / `invalid_blocks` | Message payload too large or malformed |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace admin policy blocks the action |

Tips:
- Always pass an encoded channel ID when possible; names resolve via an extra `conversations.list` call.
- Bot messages show as the bot user; to attribute a user use `as_user` with a user token (not available for bots).
- `chat.update` / `chat.delete` (scopes `chat:write`) can edit/delete messages by `channel` + `ts`.

## 8. API Limits

- `text`: 40,000 chars max
- `blocks`: 100 max per message
- File upload: 1 GB max
- `conversations.list` / `users.list` limit param: max 200
- `conversations.history` limit param: max 999
- Channel names: lowercase, max 80 chars
